title: Endpoint token runway sensitivity by model class — 2026Q3
content:
Summary:
Small working runway sheet to evaluate how many GPU slices and pool capacity we need for the Hosted API public endpoints when peak token/sec demand varies by model class. This is intentionally a sensitivity matrix (not final procurement). Use this to decide immediate prewarm targets and safety-stock planning for Q3–Q4 2026.

Key goals:
- Provide a per-region, per-model-class conversion from tokens/sec (observed and forecast) to GPUs required under three runtime profiles (baseline, optimized-quant, kv-cache-heavy).
- Show headroom targets (25% operational buffer, 75th and 95th percentile surge multipliers) and translate to reserved slices and surge slots.
- Produce quick operational recommendations: prewarm thresholds, fallback ordering, throttles.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Model classes defined as: Small (~1.5B), Medium (~7B), Large (~13B), XLarge (~70B). These align with catalog labels used by Product (see confluence link).
- Typical request length distribution (tokens per request): p50=40, p75=120, p95=450. Sequence-length sensitivity applied linearly to token/sec.
- GPU families in pool: A100-40GB (labeled a10040), H100-80GB (h10080), L40-48GB (l40). We assume mixed packing where small/medium can multiplex more KVs.
- Measured effective sustained tokens/sec per GPU (baseline runtime, no heavy quant):
  * Small: 8k tokens/sec per a10040; 12k tokens/sec per h10080; 6k per l40
  * Medium: 4.5k/a10040; 7k/h10080; 3.8k/l40
  * Large: 1.6k/a10040; 2.2k/h10080; 1.4k/l40
  * XLarge: 350/a10040; 520/h10080; 300/l40
- Optimized quant + kernel selection can improve throughput by 1.2–1.6x depending on model class; kv-cache heavy workloads can improve apparent tokens/sec for streaming long-context bursts for repeat prefixes by up to 2x for Medium/Large.
- Target SLO: p95 latency under configured model's expectation; we assume conservative GPU assignment to maintain latency SLOs under Baseline profile.

Observed baseline peak (rolling 7d peak) per region (tokens/sec observed on 2026-07-10):
- us-west: 420k tokens/sec total across all models
- us-east: 360k
- eu-west: 220k
- ap-southeast: 90k
- total-global observed peak: 1.09M tokens/sec

Forecast growth: 15% q/q for Hosted API driven by new PLG motion and increased usage from a large customer onboarding in Aug 2026. We model Q4 2026 peak baseline (no surge) = +30% over observed.

Sensitivity matrix (convert global tokens/sec to required a10040-equivalent GPUs under Baseline profile):
- Method: for a mix-weighted average throughput, we assume model-class split of requests (by tokens): Small 20%, Medium 40%, Large 30%, XLarge 10%. Compute tokens/sec contribution, divide by per-GPU tokens/sec, sum.

Example calculation (global observed 1.09M):
- Tokens by class: Small=218k, Medium=436k, Large=327k, XLarge=109k
- a10040 capacity: Small(218k/8k)=27.3, Medium(436k/4.5k)=96.9, Large(327k/1.6k)=204.4, XLarge(109k/350)=311.4 -> total ~640 a10040-equivalent GPUs (baseline).

Sensitivity table (global peak multipliers):
- Multiplier 1.0 (observed 1.09M): 640 a10040-equiv (baseline)
- Multiplier 1.25: 800 GPUs
- Multiplier 1.5: 960 GPUs
- Multiplier 2.0: 1280 GPUs

Apply runtime-optimized profile (1.3x effective improvement across mix):
- 1.0 -> 640/1.3 = ~492 a10040-equiv
- 1.25 -> ~615
- 1.5 -> ~738
- 2.0 -> ~984

Headroom policy conversions (target buffers):
- Operational buffer: +25% on top of expected capacity (reserve as hot slices to absorb noise and short bursts).
- Surge runway (for traffic spikes): maintain surge slots equal to 50% of baseline capacity (cold-mapped, can be prewarmed in 3–6 minutes with current fleet automation).
- Safety stock (procurement/committed capacity): 15% of Q4 expected baseline to cover repeated surges and regional failures.

Example end-state (Q4 forecast baseline = observed*1.30 ~1.417M tokens/sec):
- baseline GPUs (a10040-eq) under Baseline profile = 1.3x observed -> 640*1.3 ~ 832 GPUs
- +25% op buffer -> 1040 GPUs live
- +50% surge runway -> additional 416 GPUs available (cold) that can be prewarmed
- +15% safety stock -> 125 more reserved for procurement decisions
- Total procurement plane (committed) recommended ~ 1040 + 125 = 1165 GPUs with automation to add 416 prewarmable for extreme spikes.

Regional breakout (approx; convert global baseline 832 GPUs proportionally to observed regional token split):
- us-west (38.5% of observed) -> ~320 live GPUs (+25% buffer -> 400)
- us-east (33%) -> ~275 (+25% -> 344)
- eu-west (20%) -> ~166 (+25% -> 208)
- ap-southeast (8.5%) -> ~71 (+25% -> 89)

Capacity mix recommendation (to meet latency SLO + cost):
- Primary: H100 pools in us-west and us-east for medium/large workloads (mix 60% h10080, 30% a10040 for cost-effective sustained tasks, 10% l40 for cheaper embed/cheap calls).
- Deploy smaller multiplexed pools of a10040 in eu-west and ap-southeast; reserve ability to burst into cloud partner H100 capacity for short windows.

Operational playbook (short form):
- Prewarm policy: if regional 5m rolling tokens/sec > 70% of live capacity for >3 consecutive 5m windows, trigger prewarm of 20% of surge slots for that region automatically.
- Fallback ordering: Prefer falling back to quantized-medium model class for non-critical requests when region utilization exceeds 92% for 2+ minutes.
- Throttling: Implement soft-throttle at token-per-second per-customer keys with rising penalty to avoid noisy single-tenant spikes.

Open questions / risks:
- The per-GPU throughput numbers are rough: we need fresh microbenchmarks for each model variant + quantization profile. Action: Marcus to run bench suite (JIRA-1310) across h10080/a10040/l40 for prioritized 10 models by 2026-08-10.
- KV-cache effectiveness on long-session streaming is workload dependent; current 2x uplift estimate needs sampling from top-25 customers. Action: Priya to pull sample traces and run simulated caching (JIRA-1248).
- Prewarm time for H100 cold slots is variable depending on cluster health and image pull times; validate with DR run. Action: Rina to schedule DR prewarm test 2026-08-18.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Marcus Lee: run microbenchmarks for throughput matrix across GPU families and quant profiles -> 2026-08-10
- Priya Natarajan: sample 30k request traces for KV-cache effectiveness per model class -> 2026-08-05
- Rina Patel: run prewarm DR test and measure time-to-ready for h10080 pools -> 2026-08-18
- Alex Chen: update capacity plan and present at infra ops sync 2026-08-04

Notes and context links: use the confluence doc linked above for reference demand curves and the customer onboarding playbook. This sheet is purposefully conservative on latency SLOs and generous on buffers — intended for planning and procurement alignment.

Revision history (short):
- 2026-07-15 initial draft (Alex Chen)
- 2026-07-21 added runtime-optimized profile numbers (Marcus)
- 2026-08-02 appended final action items and regional splits (Alex)

Quick ask: review sensitivity assumptions and sign off on microbenchmark orders by 2026-07-30 so procurement can begin negotiating spot/backfill commitments for Q4 runway.
